judgments.reasoning_cat1: The surrender right and the termination of all coverage are clear, but the deferral sentence is mutilated ('...[six] months after receipt of your written request unless the surrender is used to pay premiums on another Policy with us'), leaving the length of the deferral to be inferred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the parallel six-month deferral for withdrawals in 5.9 and the no-reinstatement-after-surrender rule in 3.4, so the fit is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The withdrawal limits, the charge formula 'A + B + $25' with 'B' never defined, and the sentence recalculating the 'first year Surrender Fee' by dividing 'A' by the Percent of Surrender Fee are internally hard to apply as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 5.6 Cash Value, 5.7 Surrender Value, Section 1's Percent of Surrender Fee table and 6.2's Minimum Specified Amount; the Option A reduction of Specified Amount by the withdrawal plus charge is not obviously reconciled with 6.2's decrease procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lapse trigger and the grace period are stated in the same breath — the Policy 'will lapse' if Surrender Value is insufficient, yet a 60-day Grace Period is allowed during which the Policy 'continue[s] in full force' — so the moment of lapse is genuinely uncertain on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.4 states a separate lapse trigger (Cash Value over indebtedness insufficient), 5.10(2) says the Policy terminates 'without value', 3.4 allows reinstatement for five years, and 5.10's own final paragraph guarantees no lapse in the first two years; harmonising these is exactly the kind of exercise a court is asked to perform.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice obligation turns on a number of days before the end of the Grace Period that is corrupted in the text ('50 cays' against a 60-day period), and the notice is of 'the amount of premium that will be sufficient to continue the Policy in force' without saying to whom or at what address it goes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the only notice safeguard against the 5.10(2) automatic termination, and it does not connect to the reinstatement machinery in 3.4 or to any assignee/beneficiary rights under 8.3-8.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Adequate premium' is not quantified in the clause itself and 'terminate without value' is absolute; both invite argument about what payment sufficed and whether accumulated value is forfeited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is difficult to square with 3.4, which lets a lapsed policy be reinstated for five years using the values 'in effect when the Policy lapsed', and with 5.6's minimum-cash-value floor required by state law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '[A]ny premium which remains unpaid' presupposes a fixed premium obligation, which a flexible-premium policy does not impose, so the amount to be deducted is indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Under 2.9/3.2 premium is elective after the first two years, and 5.10's own trigger is a shortfall in Surrender Value rather than an unpaid premium; the deduction rule does not fit the flexible-premium architecture.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-year no-lapse guarantee states an explicit cumulative test (premiums less withdrawals less indebtedness against one-twelfth of annual Planned Periodic Premium times elapsed months); arithmetically definite, though awkwardly phrased.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides the lapse trigger in the same section and the separate trigger in 9.4, and its test differs in terms from the very similar test in 3.2(2); the precedence of the guarantee over 9.4 is not stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional statutory-basis clause naming the 1958 CSO table and 4.5% interest; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5.6's reference to state-required minimum cash values; nothing competes with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A right to request the changes 'provided for in this section' in writing; scope is expressly limited and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.4 handles changes not provided for in the section, so the two divide the field cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A heading sentence subjecting Specified Amount changes to the conditions below; purely introductory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The increase and decrease paragraphs supply the conditions; consistent with 2.12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conditions are enumerated and objective except 'application satisfactory to us' and 'evidence of insurability satisfactory to us', discretionary standards that are nonetheless conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with 3.2(4) and 6.3, which use the same insurability language, and with Section 1's minimum increase amount.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is scrambled, with the promise that the effective date 'will be shown on an addition to Section 1' displaced from the rule that the increase takes effect on the Monthly Due Date following approval.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 6.2's decrease rule and 6.3's change-of-option rule, and to 7.8's separate two-year contestability period for increases; consistent in substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive cap of one increase in any twelve months; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with 3.2(4)'s limit on increases in Planned Periodic Premium; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The ordering rule (reverse order against increases, then against the initial Specified Amount) is clear, but the final sentence about the amount 'remaining in force after any requested decrease' is cut off before its minimum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.9 imposes a Minimum Specified Amount floor after withdrawals and Section 1 states that minimum, which supplies the truncated limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause survives only in fragments and appears to permit a change from Option A to Option B while defining the new Specified Amount as 'the death benefit less the [Policy Account Value]', a formula more apt to a change from B to A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against 2.14 and 4.2, an A-to-B change with that recalculation is hard to reconcile with the definitions of the two options.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any change to your Policy that is not provided for in this section' plus the no-agent-authority sentence are broad but definite allocations of authority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 7.1's entire-contract clause and 6.1; but the officer-signature requirement also bears on the insurer's own reserved discretions in 3.2(3), 4.2 and 5.4, which are exercised without endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence omits a comma after 'This Policy', and the entire-contract statement is otherwise conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 6.4 (endorsement requirement) and with the Section 1 schedule and riders, which are physically part of the policy but not named in the entire-contract list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statements are representations 'in the absence of fraud' and only written application statements may be used to void or defend; a standard and definite allocation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 7.8 incontestability and 7.7 misstatement of age and sex, and the fraud carve-out and the two-year bar are not expressly ranked against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The later-of rule and the health-unchanged proviso are recognisable, but the clause is fragmentary and the remedy ('our liability will be to return any premium paid') is stated without saying whether coverage ever existed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 'Section 7.7 - Incontestability' when incontestability is 7.8 (7.7 is misstatement of age and sex), and the good-health proviso sits uneasily with the two-year contestability bar in 7.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-item report list; the items are specific and the only softness is item 10's garbled lapse-warning sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The items track the values defined in Sections 5 and 9, and item 10's warning complements the 5.10(1) grace-period notice without duplicating it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is truncated and leaves 'a reasonable charge as determined by us' — a charge fixed unilaterally by the drafter with no stated ceiling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same formula appears in 7.5, so it is at least used consistently within the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An illustrative-report right on written request for a reasonable charge; the assumptions sentence is cut off but the obligation is modest and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 7.4 and 7.4's extra-report right; no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The suicide clause runs 'within two years from the Issue Date', a term the policy nowhere defines, and limits liability to premium refunded less indebtedness and withdrawals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2 defines Policy Date and Effective Date but not Issue Date, and 7.2 keys effect to the later of Policy Date or premium payment; the measuring date must be imported from elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only fragments of the misstatement-of-age-and-sex rule survive, so the adjustment mechanism ('based on the [amount the cost of insurance paid] would have provided, at the correct age and sex') cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on 5.4, where COI depends on sex, age and risk class, and on 7.8, which bars contest after two years but says nothing about age adjustment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The incontestability promise carries an exception — 'unless the Surrender Value is insufficient to cover the next Monthly Cost of Insurance' — which is not a contestability concept at all and uses a charge label ('Monthly Cost of Insurance') found nowhere else.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That exception effectively re-imports the 5.10/9.4 lapse triggers into a clause about contesting the policy, and it measures from an undefined 'Issue Date' rather than the Policy Date of 2.6 or the Effective Date of 7.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A separate two-year contestability period for increases; short and definite once the corrupted words are restored.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 6.2's increase machinery and the first paragraph of 7.8; the two periods run independently, as intended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line non-participation statement; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cover page description 'NONPARTICIPATING' and with the absence of any dividend provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Taken literally, the Owner may exercise rights only if there is no irrevocable beneficiary and the Policy has not been assigned, which would strip the Owner of every right the moment either condition fails rather than merely qualifying them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.3 says only that the Owner's rights are 'subject to any assignment', and 8.2/8.4 assume the Owner can still act after assignment or an irrevocable designation; the absolute condition here does not sit easily with those.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change-of-ownership mechanics survive only in pieces (written notice, effective on signing, no effect on prior payments, policy may be required for endorsement), so the clause as reproduced is incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the change-of-beneficiary rule in 8.4 almost exactly, so the missing words are recoverable from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment is permitted, is not binding until written notice, and the insurer disclaims validity; each limb is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies 8.1's condition that the Policy 'has not been assigned' and subordinates revocable beneficiary rights, which is the reconciling gloss 8.1 lacks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The default (Owner is beneficiary if none named) and the source (the application) are clear; 'except as provided in this section' is an express internal cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.4 and with 4.1's direction that Death Proceeds go to the Beneficiary; Section 1 simply says 'AS SPECIFIED ON THE [application]'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The survivorship and default-to-Owner cascade is stated step by step and is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.1 and 4.1; nothing else addresses predeceasing beneficiaries.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '[E]ffective upon the date your request was signed but will have no effect on any payment made or other action taken by us before we receive it' is a well-worn relation-back formula, definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks 8.2's change-of-ownership rule and is expressly subject to an irrevocable designation, matching 8.1's condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The loan right is reduced to a fragment ('You may obtain a Policy [loan] ... us is the only security needed'), so the conditions on borrowing are not visible in the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9.2 supplies the amount available and 9.4 the consequences, so the missing terms are largely recoverable from the rest of Section 9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The loan-availability formula lost its base ('The amount [available is the Surrender Value] less: 1. loan interest to the next Policy anniversary; and 2. Monthly Insurance Charges for the balance of the Policy year'), so the starting figure is missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the base is Cash Value or Surrender Value matters under 5.6, 5.7 and 9.4, and the instrument does not resolve it here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest accrues from the date of the loan at the Section 1 rate, is payable annually, and unpaid interest is added to the loan; each step is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.4's definition of indebtedness and with 5.2's reduced crediting rate on loaned account value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause defines indebtedness clearly but ends with an independent lapse rule expressed as 'the excess of the Cash Value over the total Policy Indebtedness' being insufficient for the next Monthly Insurance Charges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That is a second lapse trigger sitting outside Section 5.10, with no grace period, no 5.10(1) notice and no reference to the two-year no-lapse guarantee; whether 5.10's protections attach to a 9.4 lapse is a genuine internal question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is fragmented, with the payee identification and the 'subject to Section 8' qualifier severed from the list of options they govern.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8 governs ownership, assignment and beneficiaries, so the qualifier is at least directed at a real part of the instrument; Options 1-5 supply the choices.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sum payment at the date of claim settlement; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1 and 10.2; no competing provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence collapses two alternatives ('either for a specified period or for a specified amount') into a garbled present-value clause, leaving the mechanics of the fixed-amount branch unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Fixed Period table that follows covers only the specified-period branch, and 10.2 requires present value equal to the Proceeds, so the fixed-amount alternative is left without machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The illustrative figures contain plain numerical errors — '$6,384' for a monthly income per $1,000 and a ''0 year' guaranteed minimum period — that misstate the guarantee on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Payments for Life table gives the male age-65 rates as 6.72 and (for certain periods) lower figures, which do not match the 6.77/6.38 stated here; the two need reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The joint-life option survives only in fragments, with the opening ('We will pay a monthly income during the lifetime of two payees') cut away and the guarantee sentence broken.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Unlike Option 3, no guaranteed table is supplied and rates are 'furnished upon request', which is consistent with 10.2 but leaves the guarantee unverifiable within the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The interest option is reduced to fragments and the withdrawal limitation ('unless the B[eneficiary Designation] limits withdrawals, any withdrawal must [be at least...]') is incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A beneficiary designation limiting withdrawals interacts with 8.4's change-of-beneficiary machinery, but nothing in Section 8 expressly authorises such settlement restrictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '[O]ur rates in effect at the time of settlement' plus a present-value equality is a definite, if insurer-favourable, rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Options 2, 3 and 4 each promise rates 'never less than the guaranteed rates', so a current-rate rule here must be read as a floor rather than a ceiling; the ranking is implicit rather than stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence saying other payment frequencies are available on request; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the monthly tables and 10.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of guaranteed periods is corrupted ('not less than % 10, Ss, -or 20 yegrs'), so the elective certain periods cannot be read off the clause itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The adjoining table supplies the columns (no certain period, 5, 10, 15 and 20 years), which repairs the list; Option 3 uses the same structure.
